questions.question: Identify the reason for formation of dental plaque.

options.text: When acids stick to the teeth
Masses of bacterial cells together with food particles stick to the teeth
When bacteria acting on sugars produce acids

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Masses of bacterial cells together with food particles stick to the teeth**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Masses of bacterial cells together with food particles stick to the teeth** are the primary reason for the formation of dental plaque.
 
• Dental plaque is a sticky, colorless or pale yellow film that is constantly forming on your teeth.
 
• Plaque is made up of bacteria and food particles. When you consume foods or drinks that contain sugars or starches, the bacteria in plaque produce acids that attack tooth enamel.
 
• If plaque is not removed by regular brushing and flossing, it can harden into tartar (calculus), which can lead to gum disease and cavities.
 
• Maintaining good oral hygiene by brushing twice a day, flossing daily, and visiting the dentist regularly can help prevent the formation of plaque and tartar.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Saliva** helps to wash away food particles and neutralize acids produced by bacteria in the mouth, which helps to protect against plaque buildup.
 
• **Fluoride**, found in many dental products and drinking water, helps to strengthen tooth enamel and prevent decay.
 
• **Regular dental check-ups** can help identify and treat plaque and tartar buildup before it leads to more serious dental issues.
 
• Some **foods and beverages**, such as sugary snacks and drinks, can contribute to plaque formation and should be consumed in moderation.
 
• Using **antibacterial mouthwash** can also help reduce the number of bacteria in the mouth that contribute to plaque formation.

questions.question: Which of the following diseases is detected by the Widal test?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Typhoid**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Widal test** is a serological test used to detect the presence of antibodies against **Salmonella Typhi**, the causative agent of typhoid fever.
 
• It measures agglutination (clumping) of antigens and antibodies in the patient’s serum to diagnose **enteric fever** (typhoid and paratyphoid).
 
• This test identifies the **O (somatic) and H (flagellar)** antigens of Salmonella Typhi and Salmonella Paratyphi.
 
• The Widal test is especially useful in endemic regions where typhoid fever is common.
 
• A significant rise in antibody titers between two samples taken 7–10 days apart confirms active infection.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Typhoid Fever:**

 
 
• Typhoid is a bacterial infection caused by **Salmonella Typhi**, transmitted through contaminated food or water.
 
• Symptoms include prolonged fever, abdominal pain, weakness, loss of appetite, and sometimes a rash called "rose spots."
 
• Preventive measures include vaccination, safe drinking water, and proper sanitation.
 
 
 
• **Widal Test Procedure:**
 
 
• The patient’s blood sample is collected, and the serum is separated.
 
• The serum is mixed with antigen suspensions of Salmonella Typhi and observed for agglutination.
 
• A titer of 1:160 or higher is generally considered significant in endemic areas.
 
 
 
• **Limitations of Widal Test:**
 
 
• It may produce false positives due to prior vaccination or cross-reactivity with other infections.
 
• It is less reliable in the early stages of infection as antibody levels take time to rise.
 
 
 
• **Alternate Diagnostic Methods:**
 
 
• Blood culture is the gold standard for diagnosing typhoid fever but requires specialized lab facilities.
 
• Rapid diagnostic tests (RDTs) are also available, but their sensitivity and specificity vary.

questions.question: Which set of diseases are caused by bacteria?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Typhoid, Cholera, Tuberculosis**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Typhoid fever is caused by the bacterium **Salmonella typhi** and is typically spread through contaminated food and water.
 
• Cholera is caused by the bacterium **Vibrio cholerae** and is also usually spread through contaminated water and food, leading to severe diarrhea and dehydration.
 
• Tuberculosis (TB) is caused by the bacterium **Mycobacterium tuberculosis** and primarily affects the lungs, but can also affect other parts of the body.
 
• These diseases are treatable with antibiotics, which target and kill the bacterial pathogens responsible for the infections.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Influenza**

 
 
• Influenza, also known as the flu, is caused by influenza viruses, not bacteria.
 
• It is a contagious respiratory illness with symptoms like fever, cough, and body aches.
 
• Vaccines are available to help prevent influenza.
 
 
 
• **Dengue**
 
 
• Dengue is caused by the dengue virus, which is transmitted by Aedes mosquitoes.
 
• It leads to symptoms such as high fever, severe headache, pain behind the eyes, joint and muscle pain, and rash.
 
• There is no specific treatment for dengue, but supportive care can help manage symptoms.
 
 
 
• **Malaria**
 
 
• Malaria is caused by Plasmodium parasites, which are transmitted through the bites of infected Anopheles mosquitoes.
 
• Symptoms include fever, chills, and flu-like illness; if not treated, it can lead to severe complications and death.
 
• Antimalarial drugs are used to treat and prevent malaria.
 
 
 
• **Common Cold**
 
 
• The common cold is caused by a variety of viruses, most commonly rhinoviruses.
 
• It is characterized by symptoms such as sneezing, runny nose, and sore throat.
 
• There is no cure for the common cold, but symptoms can be managed with over-the-counter medications.

questions.question: Which disease refers to the inflammation of the liver caused by a variety of infectious viruses and non-infectious agents leading to a variety of health problems?

They're normally harmless or even helpful. But under **certain conditions**, **some organisms **may **cause disease**. Some **infectious diseases **can be **passed from person to person**.
 
• **Hepatitis **means **inflammation **of **the liver**. The **liver **is **a vital organ **that **processes nutrients**, **filters the blood**, and **fights infections**. When the liver is **inflamed or damaged**, its **function **can be **affected**.

Not everyone **infected **with **TB bacteria **becomes **sick**.

The **infection **can be **life-threatening **to anyone, but particularly to **infants, children, **and **people over 65**. **Symptoms **include **a cough **with **phlegm or pus**, **fever**, **chills**, and **difficulty breathing**.

questions.question: Which of the following terms, also known as hypersensitivity, is used to describe a condition in which the human body has an exaggerated response to a substance (e.g. food or drug)?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Allergy**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Allergy **also known as **hypersensitivity,** is used to describe a condition in which the human body has an exaggerated response to a substance (e.g. food or drug).
 
• **Hypersensitive (also known as hypersensitivity reaction or intolerance) **refers to the immune system's unfavourable reactions, such as allergies and autoimmunity.
 
• These reactions are commonly referred to as an immune system overreaction, and they can be harmful and unpleasant.
 
• This is an immunologic phrase that should not be confused with the psychiatric term hypersensitivity, which refers to someone who is highly sensitive to physical (sound, touch, light, etc.) and/or emotional stimuli.
 
• **Pollen, moulds, animal dander, latex, certain foods, and insect stings **are examples of generally harmless substances that can cause allergies.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **An infection** is the infiltration of disease-causing pathogens into an organism's bodily tissues, their multiplication, and the host tissues' reaction to the infectious agents and the toxins they create.
 
• **A mutation **is a change in an organism's DNA sequence. Mutations can occur as a result of mistakes in DNA replication during cell division, mutagen exposure, or viral infection.
 
• People use the term **"convulsion"** to describe involuntary muscle contractions.

questions.question:
Which of the following pairs of 'disease – duration' is correct?

I. Acute – long duration

II. Chronic – short time
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Option 1**__. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The correct pairing of 'disease - duration' is:
 
 
• **Acute - short time**
 
• ** Chronic - long duration**
 
 
 
• **Acute diseases** are characterized by a sudden onset and a relatively short duration. They typically resolve within a short period, ranging from a few days to a few weeks. Examples of acute diseases include the common cold, acute bronchitis, and acute appendicitis.
 
• On the other hand, **chronic diseases** are characterized by a long duration, typically lasting for months or years. They often develop slowly and persist over an extended period, sometimes for a person's lifetime. Examples of chronic diseases include diabetes, hypertension (high blood pressure), and rheumatoid arthritis.
 
• Therefore, the correct pairing would be **"Acute - short time" and "Chronic - long duration."**

questions.question: Which antibiotic is considered the first miracle drug, used to treat throat infections, meningitis, syphilis and other bacterial infections?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Penicillin**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Penicillin** is considered the first miracle drug.
 
• It was discovered by Alexander Fleming in 1928 and became widely used in the 1940s.
 
• Penicillin is effective against a wide range of bacterial infections, including throat infections, meningitis, and syphilis.
 
• Its discovery marked the beginning of modern antibiotics and has saved countless lives.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Penicillin** works by interfering with the ability of bacteria to form cell walls, leading to their destruction.
 
• It was first mass-produced during World War II, playing a critical role in treating infections among soldiers.
 
• Penicillin has led to the development of other antibiotics, transforming medical treatment of bacterial infections.
 
• Despite its effectiveness, some bacteria have developed resistance to penicillin, highlighting the need for ongoing research in antibiotic development.

questions.question: Which of the following is a mineral deficiency disease?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Goitre**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Goitre** is a condition characterized by the abnormal enlargement of the thyroid gland.
 
• It is most commonly caused by an iodine deficiency, which is an essential mineral for thyroid hormone production.
 
• The condition is often seen in areas where the diet is deficient in iodine, such as mountainous regions.
 
• Goitre can lead to symptoms like swelling in the neck, difficulty breathing or swallowing, and hypothyroidism or hyperthyroidism.
 
• Prevention includes ensuring adequate iodine intake through iodized salt or iodine supplements.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Thyroid Gland**

 
 
• The thyroid gland is located in the neck and produces hormones that regulate metabolism, growth, and development.
 
• It uses iodine from the diet to produce thyroid hormones, primarily thyroxine (T4) and triiodothyronine (T3).
 
• Thyroid hormone levels are crucial for normal brain development, especially during the early stages of life.
 
 
 
• **Iodine Deficiency**
 
 
• Iodine is a trace mineral found in certain foods and is necessary for the production of thyroid hormones.
 
• Deficiency can lead to various health issues, including goitre, hypothyroidism, and developmental abnormalities in children.
 
• Marine foods, dairy products, and iodized salt are good sources of dietary iodine.
 
 
 
• **Hypothyroidism**
 
 
• It is a condition where the thyroid gland does not produce enough thyroid hormones.
 
• Symptoms include fatigue, weight gain, cold intolerance, and depression.
 
• Treatment typically involves hormone replacement therapy with synthetic thyroxine (T4).
 
 
 
• **Hyperthyroidism**
 
 
• It is a condition where the thyroid gland produces excess thyroid hormones.
 
• Symptoms include weight loss, rapid heartbeat, sweating, and irritability.
 
• Treatment may involve antithyroid medications, radioactive iodine therapy, or surgery.

• The main symptom of elephantiasis is gross enlargement and swelling of an area of the body because of the accumulation of fluid. The arms and legs are the areas most often affected. An entire arm or leg may swell to several times its normal size resembling the thick, round appearance of an elephant's leg.

• Many of them are soil-transmitted intestinal worms that infect the gastrointestinal tract.

• **Sleeping sickness**, also known as **African trypanosomiasis**, is caused by **protozoa of the genus Trypanosoma**.
 
• It is transmitted to human hosts through the **bite of infected tsetse flies**, which are found in sub-Saharan Africa.
 
• The disease is characterized by two stages: the first stage involves fever, headaches, joint pains, and itching, while the second stage affects the central nervous system, leading to neurological symptoms such as confusion, sensory disturbances, and poor coordination.
 
• Without treatment, sleeping sickness can be fatal, highlighting the importance of early diagnosis and intervention.

questions.question: Which is a serious contagious bacterial infection that usually affects the mucous membranes of the nose and throat?

• The disease is caused by the bacterium Corynebacterium diphtheriae*.
 
• Diphtheria spreads through respiratory droplets from coughing or sneezing.
 
• Symptoms include a thick, gray membrane covering the throat and tonsils, sore throat, swollen glands, and difficulty breathing.

• **Meningococcal Disease**

 
 
• Meningococcal disease is caused by the bacterium Neisseria meningitidis*.
 
• It can lead to serious infections such as meningitis (inflammation of the membranes around the brain and spinal cord) and septicemia (blood poisoning).
 
• The disease spreads through respiratory droplets and close contact with an infected person.
 
• Symptoms include sudden fever, headache, and a stiff neck, often accompanied by nausea, vomiting, sensitivity to light, and altered mental status.

• Shigellosis is an infectious disease caused by a group of bacteria called *Shigella*.
 
• It is characterized by diarrhea (often bloody), fever, and stomach cramps.
 
• The infection spreads through contaminated food, water, or contact with an infected person.
 
• Good hygiene practices, especially handwashing, are critical for preventing the spread of Shigellosis.
 
 
 
• **Chlamydia**
 
 
• Chlamydia is a common sexually transmitted infection (STI) caused by the bacterium *Chlamydia trachomatis*.
 
• It can infect both men and women, causing damage to the reproductive system.
 
• Symptoms may include abnormal genital discharge and a burning sensation during urination.
 
• If left untreated, Chlamydia can lead to serious reproductive and other health problems with both short-term and long-term consequences.
